name: Elihu
overview: Elihu is a male figure from the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Jeroham and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel. His lineage places him within the Levitical heritage, which is significant in the biblical narrative. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond these familial connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Elihu means 'y-h-v-h is [my] God,' reflecting a personal declaration of faith in the LORD. This name is distinct from related Levitical names such as Eliab ('God is my father') and Eliel ('God is my God'), which also emphasize devotion to God. These names collectively highlight the spiritual identity of this Levitical family line.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Elihu is the father of Jeroham and explicitly the father of Tohu, indicating his role as a patriarch within his family. These relationships situate him as an important ancestor, notably connected to Samuel, the prophet, through his son Jeroham. No other family relationships are documented in the given data.
scriptureSignificance: Elihu's significance lies in his position within the Levitical lineage as an ancestor of Samuel, a key prophet in Israel's history. His role as father to Jeroham connects him to the priestly heritage that undergirded Samuel's prophetic ministry. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, Elihu's genealogical placement underscores God's providential preparation of Samuel's lineage for service to His covenant people.
